findings.location: PreparedCodeGraphWorkspaceOwnership and UseOwnedStateAsync; plan.md ID-I07, ID-S06 and ID-T06
findings.affected_requirement: spec FR-012 and SC-007; Story 18.3 positive reader binding
findings.evidence: The contract makes PreparedCodeGraphWorkspaceOwnership an immutable record with a nullable StateEntryObjectIdentity. Null is valid only before exclusive creation; an owned entry and later leases require the recorded non-null physical identity. UseOwnedStateAsync returns only PreparedToolWorkspaceCheckStatus, its short-lived scope exposes a path but no ownership transition, and the coordinator injects only read verifiers. No callable producer or commit handoff updates and retains the record after creating .codegraph. A post-create check using the still-null record conflicts with the stated owned-entry invariant; later leases, Story 18.3's reader and restart cannot obtain the required verified positive binding. The disposition contract also leaves the ownership record's transition to removed state unspecified for its post-check.
findings.correction_outcome: Define one internal trusted record transition that captures and retains the exclusively created entry identity, verifies it before use, makes a current verified view available to Story 18.3, and records or quarantines partial creation and terminal disposition. Keep the coordinator and ownership authority in Story 18.2, without name-only adoption or a second reader contract.

raw_result.summary: Plan-only REVISE. P-CODEGRAPH-DISPOSITION-AUTHORITY-01 is resolved: disposal now receives a matching trusted current approval and has the existing source and CodeGraph-purpose verifiers, owner/readiness checks, post-checks and quarantine behavior. Earlier PATH trust, launch order, partial-open ownership and runtime-settings findings remain resolved. The new concrete ownership record has no specified transition from pre-create to verified post-create identity, preventing the positive binding required by later leases and Story 18.3. The stable root-object decision preserves replacement denial in the plan while leaving Story 18.1's reader policy and JDT's separate state intact. Native child confinement, ordinary-reader repair and real JDT qualification remain unverified dependencies.
